verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 16.6
verses.english: Linked Discourses 16.6

verses.pali: 1. Kassapavagga
verses.english: 1. Kassapa

verses.pali: Ovādasutta
verses.english: Advice

verses.pali: Rājagahe veḷuvane.
verses.english: Near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Venerable Mahākassapa went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

verses.pali: “ovada, kassapa, bhikkhū;
verses.english: “Kassapa, advise the mendicants!

verses.pali: karohi, kassapa, bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiṁ kathaṁ.
verses.english: Give them a Dhamma talk!

verses.pali: Ahaṁ vā, kassapa, bhikkhū ovadeyyaṁ tvaṁ vā;
verses.english: Either you or I should advise the mendicants

verses.pali: ahaṁ vā bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiṁ kathaṁ kareyyaṁ tvaṁ vā”ti.
verses.english: and give them a Dhamma talk.”

verses.pali: “Dubbacā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhū, dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, akkhamā, appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṁ.
verses.english: “Sir, the mendicants these days are hard to admonish, having qualities that make them hard to admonish. They’re impatient, and don’t take instruction respectfully.

verses.pali: Idhāhaṁ, bhante, addasaṁ bhaṇḍañca nāma bhikkhuṁ ānandassa saddhivihāriṁ abhijikañca nāma bhikkhuṁ anuruddhassa saddhivihāriṁ aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadante:
verses.english: Take the monk named Bhaṇḍa, Ānanda’s protégé. He’s been competing in studies with the monk named Abhiñjika, Anuruddha’s protégé. They say:

verses.pali: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’”ti.
verses.english: ‘Come on, monk, who can speak more? Who can speak better? Who can speak longer?’”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,

verses.pali: “ehi tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena bhaṇḍañca bhikkhuṁ ānandassa saddhivihāriṁ abhijikañca bhikkhuṁ anuruddhassa saddhivihāriṁ āmantehi:
verses.english: “Please, monk, in my name tell the monk called Bhaṇḍa, Ānanda’s protégé, and the monk called Abhiñjika, Anuruddha’s protégé that

verses.pali: ‘satthā āyasmante āmantetī’”ti.
verses.english: the teacher summons them.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca:
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” that monk replied. He went to those monks and said,

verses.pali: “satthā āyasmante āmantetī”ti.
verses.english: “Venerables, the teacher summons you.”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: “Yes, reverend,” those monks replied. They went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to them:

verses.pali: “saccaṁ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadatha:
verses.english: “Is it really true, monks, that you’ve been competing in studies, saying:

verses.pali: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’”ti?
verses.english: ‘Come on, monk, who can speak more? Who can speak better? Who can speak longer?’”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Yes, sir.”

verses.pali: “Kiṁ nu kho me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṁ dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānātha:
verses.english: “Have you ever known me to teach the Dhamma like this:

verses.pali: ‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadatha—
verses.english: ‘Please mendicants, compete in studies to

verses.pali: ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’”ti?
verses.english: see who can recite more and better and longer’?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “No, sir.”

verses.pali: “No ce kira me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṁ dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānātha, atha kiñcarahi tumhe, moghapurisā, kiṁ jānantā kiṁ passantā evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadatha:
verses.english: “If you’ve never known me to teach the Dhamma like this, what then do you know and see, you futile men, that after going forth in such a well explained teaching and training you’d compete in studies to

verses.pali: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’”ti.
verses.english: see who can speak more and better and longer?”

verses.pali: Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then those monks bowed with their heads at the Buddha’s feet and said,

verses.pali: “accayo no, bhante, accagamā, yathābāle yathāmūḷhe yathāakusale, ye mayaṁ evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadimha:
verses.english: “We made a mistake, sir. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of us in that after going forth in such a well explained teaching and training we competed in studies to

verses.pali: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’ti.
verses.english: see who can speak more and better and longer.

verses.pali: Tesaṁ no, bhante, bhagavā accayaṁ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṁ saṁvarāyā”ti.
verses.english: Please, sir, accept our mistake for what it is, so we will restrain ourselves in future.”

verses.pali: “Taggha tumhe, bhikkhave, accayo accagamā yathābāle yathāmūḷhe yathāakusale, ye tumhe evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadittha:
verses.english: “Indeed, monks, you made a mistake. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of you to act in that way.

verses.pali: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’ti.
Yato ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikarotha, taṁ vo mayaṁ paṭiggaṇhāma.
verses.english: But since you have recognized your mistake for what it is, and have dealt with it properly, I accept it.

verses.pali: Vuddhi hesā, bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikaroti āyatiñca saṁvaraṁ āpajjatī”ti.
verses.english: For it is growth in the training of the Noble One to recognize a mistake for what it is, deal with it properly, and commit to restraint in the future.”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
